payload.fact: At STG Logistics, each emailed-tender order took about five minutes and at least 45 fields, yet 15 people spent 60% of their day on the work; Pallet says its system now creates 95% of processed orders without manual field entry.
payload.expected: A five-minute administrative task would be too small to matter strategically.
payload.actual: Repeated at scale across variable files and 45 fields, it consumed most of 15 people's workday.
payload.tension: The unit task looked trivial while its aggregate labor was enormous.
payload.target: The decision habit of dismissing repetitive administrative work because each instance is short.
payload.reader_realization: Small tasks become large systems when volume and variability compound.

angles.line: The five-minute task became 60% of the day for 15 people.
One order looked like five minutes of admin; the same process at scale looked like most of a department's day.
Every variable tender became at least 45 more fields for someone to key in.
The automation target was not the form but the messy handoff that kept recreating it.
The vendor's 95% automation claim leaves the other 5% and its checking cost outside the frame.
